She took the bronze medal in the Commonwealth Games in Manchester, was a finalist in the European Championships in Munich, and still found time to compete in Southern League and Cup Final teams.

Shelley Newman took bronze in the discus; bronze went to Vernicha James who ran in the sprint relay; high jumper Ben Challenger began to scale the heights again - and won bronze; Phillips Idowu produced a massive leap in the triple jump to lead the competition but ultimately take silver, Sean Baldoc…
Above right: Setting new Belgrave standards in all that she does, Shelley Newman became Belgrave's first ever female medallist at a Commonwealth Games, taking bronze in the discus with 58m 13cm.

Now turning to individual performances, in the major worldwide championships, seven Belgravians qualified for the World Athletic Championships; Sean Baldock, Tim Benjamin, Dwain Chambers, (who achieved a silver medal in the 4 x 100 m), Julie Hollman, Rachel King, Shelley Newman and Amy Spencer.
Shelley Newman in the outside throwing area did not seem to be distracted by the regular passage of cars behind the cage on the way to the overflow car park and managed 55.42 metres.
Shelley Newman was fourth in the hammer (26.61) and second in the B shot (10.96) but let us know that she is the UK No 1 in the discus with 54.65 metres.
